learning_outcomes.text: Identify the different types of errors that can be made when using numerical methods and compare their efficiency according to the type of problem to be solved, the required degree of precision, and the computational cost.
Evaluate and use the most appropriate methods to detect the roots of a non-linear equation.
Describe, analyze, and use numerical methods for solving systems of linear and non-linear equations.
Numerically solve problems of interpolation, one-dimensional data fitting, and function approximation.
Use formulas to approximately obtain the definite integral of a function.
Describe, use, and evaluate basic numerical methods for solving optimization problems.

syllabus_topics: Numerical methods for solving linear and non-linear systems.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum score of 3.5 out of 10 is required for both the theoretical and practical blocks. The theoretical block score is calculated as (0.45 x T1) + (0.45 x T2) + (0.10 x TP), and the practical block score as (0.25 x P1) + (0.25 x P2) + (0.5 x L). If all minimums are met and laboratory attendance is 80% or higher, the final grade is (0.6 x Theory) + (0.4 x Practices). Otherwise, the grade is the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, a theoretical exam and a practical exam are given, each requiring a minimum of 3.5 out of 10. The final grade is calculated using the same formula as the ordinary call if minimums are met, otherwise it is the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0.
